classification.difficultyReason: Introduce the equilateral triangle's altitude and express its half-base in terms of its unknown side, solve the resulting equation, then transfer that side to the square and derive the legs needed for NK.

content.prompt: JKML is a square. Determine the length of $NK$ if the height of the triangle $\Delta NML$ is 24 cm. Answer to two decimal places.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12, square diagram below the stem on the left
spec.description: Square JKML containing equilateral triangle NML. JN and KN join the upper vertices to N. S is on KM level with N, with NS perpendicular to SK. Retains all six filled point markers, three equal-side ticks and three 60-degree angle labels.
spec.mathematics: For square side s, L=(0,0), M=(s,0), J=(0,s), K=(s,s), N=(s/2,sqrt(3)s/2) and S=(s,sqrt(3)s/2). Triangle NML is equilateral. Diagram coordinates express these relationships without printing additional measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: All source givens remain visible; no calculated lengths or solution-only construction is shown.

answer.worked:
Split equilateral triangle $NML$ vertically down the middle. Each resulting right-angled triangle has height 24 cm and base half the side length. Let $NM=x$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}
\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^2+24^2&=x^2\\
\frac{x^2}{4}+24^2&=x^2\\
24^2&=\frac{3x^2}{4}\\
x^2&=768\\
x&=\sqrt{768}
\end{align*}$$
The square has side length $\sqrt{768}$ cm. Also, $SM=24$ cm and $NS$ is half the square's side.
$$\begin{align*}
KS&=KM-SM\\
KS&=\sqrt{768}-24\\
NS&=\frac{\sqrt{768}}{2}\\
NK&=\sqrt{\left(\sqrt{768}-24\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{768}}{2}\right)^2}\\
NK&\approx14.35\text{ cm}
\end{align*}$$
